It was great to see Darren Mead back in action over the country for the Bels. while 24 year-old Lee Hurst, on his début, took the chance to measure himself up against some of the London Lads.
Gary was back in the squad, returning from his pre-Christmas complete layoff. Lee Hurst was down from Manchester and raring to go while Roger Alsop and Jim Estall were known to be in cracking form.

At Clayton Vale, over 7 miles, the Greater Manchester Championships gave Lee Hurst the chance to fly the Belgrave flag. He finished just 3 seconds outside the medals as Sale's Kevin McKay grabbed 3rd in 36:49 to the Belgravian's 36:52.
Anyway, let's stop whinging and savour a fine run by Lee Hurst. Around 20th after the first loop, Lee worked his way through some of the top runners from the South of England.

Only Rob Denmark was able to run a faster short stage time on the day than our Mark. Now, could Lee Hurst get us into the frame? He had already had an exciting afternoon.

A strong contender for the National team, Lee Hurst put his neck on the block by turning out among the club men and immediately earned their respect and a club record for this circuit as he took Belgrave up to 7th with an 18:22 timing.

Stage Three: It was up to Lee Hurst to take us to the half-way point. He'd been churning out some solid race performances recently and another good effort came from him here as he picked off seven men to move the Bels up the field.
Our team was depleted when Mark Miles fell foul of a cold, Paul Freary opted to race in Bermuda and Lee Hurst decided to concentrate on the Southern the following week.

Paul Freary headed the field of nigh-on 1,000 runners as they reached the summit of the first climb and as he looked across to track the progress of any rivals he could see the claret and gold vest of his clubmate Lee Hurst also claiming an early forward place.
Three in five ... but this was nothing, for after a very short gap came Paul Freary 6th, Lee Hurst 8th, the bandana'd Charles Herrington 9th and then Kevin Nash and Alaster Stewart inside the dozen.

Lee Hurst was now our leading man in 44th, Paul Freary 52nd, Jason Lobo 60th Charles Herrington 70th, Kevin Nash 76th and Alaster Stewart 95th - a score of just under 400 and already a set of medals looked unlikely.
If Alaster Stewart could only stop Tipton's Nigel Stirk from getting past then man for man we believed that our own Lee Hurst would be able to look after the last leg.

Enjoying the chance to steer as clear of stage 12 as possible, Lee Hurst was given the target of a place in the teens and although he was a little disappointed with his time, his 17th spot in 27:13 - place and time - was exactly what had been predicted by Vice-Captain Al Stewart.
